messages:
eli: kicking off onboarding for orwell12b int4. canary started on A10G. seeing a pattern: OOMs mid-decode ~600-900 tokens when sessions hit second turn (session cache warm). attaching short repro.

mira: can you paste runtime + args? sounds like session cache priming might double-allocate KV in some codepath.

eli: runtime v2.3.4, kernel=fast-attn-v2, args:
```
--quant int4 --prefetch=true --session_cache=true --batch_size=12 --max_new_tokens=1024 --kv_reserve=0.14
```
log snip:
```
[2026-03-25T13:05:02Z] session cache prime start for session s123
[2026-03-25T13:05:02Z] alloc slab stripe 64->192MB
[2026-03-25T13:05:03Z] GPU alloc fail 48MB -> OOM during decode
[2026-03-25T13:05:03Z] fallback: kernel_v1_path queued for request r456
```

dom: repro script? node type?

eli: repro: https://internal/ci/repro/orwell-session-repro.sh. A10G nodes. can repro locally with 3 concurrent two-turn conversations (first turn ~400 tokens, second turn ~800 tokens).

mira: hypothesis: session_cache prime triggers additional KV prefetch that runs before previous request's compaction finishes, causing slab spike. also kernel fast-attn-v2 has more aggressive prefetch heuristics.

dom: short mitigations:
- disable session_cache priming for int4 canary (cheap toggle)
- reduce batch_size to 8
- increase kv_reserve to 0.22 for sessioned requests
- add kernel fallback on alloc fail (already happening) but make it faster by short-circuit requeue instead of full retry

eli: applied local patch: session_cache_prime=false for canary, batch_size=8, kv_reserve=0.22. repro runs: 0 OOMs/1000, p95 latency +11% on second-turns.

mira: good. longer term: two ideas:
1) change session cache prime to incremental/streaming priming (prime only a few layers ahead) to smooth allocations
2) make prefetch stagger relative to session activity so priming waves don't sync across sessions
dom: agree. also add a runtime metric: session_prime_inflight_count and prime_offset_ms. canary dashboards should show these.

ci-bot: created CI job orwell-session-prime-smoke. test: 20 two-turn conversations concurrency 3. thresholds: 0 OOMs, p95 <= baseline*1.25.

eli: added flag patch: runtime.flags.session_prime_mode=incremental with window_ms=200 and runtime.flags.prefetch_stagger=enabled. tested locally: 0 OOMs, p95 +9% but much lower slab tail.

mira: schedule A/B for quality and perf: A=baseline int8, B=int4+incremental-prime+stagger, C=int4+no-prime (the temporary safe path). Run token-acc on long conversational QA set.

dom: also instrument per-request allocation timeline so we can see which op caused the OOM. important for triage.

ops-bot: alert rule added: orwell-session-prime-oom -> page on any OOM in canary for 10m. dashboard tiles: session_prime_inflight, slab_stripe_by_node, prime_offset_distribution.

eli: rolling config to canary cohort 4% with incremental prime + stagger. PR: https://internal/pr/4720. will monitor.

mira: fallback strategy agreed: on alloc fail, fast-requeue to kernel_v1 path with original request metadata; if the request is sessioned and session_prime=false, route to int8 variant. document in runbook.

dom: follow-ups: eng-runtime ticket to implement streaming prime with configurable layer-chunk (ENG-RT-1134), and a perf microbench for prime window sizing.

ci-bot: smoke started. initial telemetry: slab spikes reduced 38%, session_prime_inflight avg dropped to 1.2, no OOMs in first 30m. p95 second-turn +9%. CI smoke running.

eli: will keep canary pinned and watch for 2h. if smoke passes and nightly A/B quality shows token-acc delta <=2% vs int8, expand to 20% and enable per-session adaptive kv_reserve.

mira: thanks. documenting lessons: session priming can double memory footprint transiently; prefer incremental prime and stagger to avoid allocator storms. will add to onboarding checklist. :memo:

eli: closing thread for now. will post results after CI and nightly. thanks all. :rocket:
